$comment: Source rows that no research pass recorded, added because a corpus source reads them. `buildSourceRegister` reads each row after the research CSV's rows, in the CSV's own columns, so its id and license scope come from the same derivation. A row a corpus source reads records `CORPUS INPUT, TERMS UNREAD`, which derives an `unchecked` decision: the row exists so that the gap shows in the register rather than hiding as an absence. A row whose terms were read when it was added records the access label `Free` instead. Among them are publications no corpus source reads: Poste Maroc's and 4-72's post-office lists, whose share-alike grants the share-alike-free license policy refuses; UN/LOCODE, which `@mailwoman/un-locode-lookup` builds a lookup from; and OurAirports, which `@mailwoman/registry` compiles its airport codes from. Each records that outcome in its decision. A decision is recorded in `license-decisions.json` like any other. See `corpus-source-inputs.json` for which corpus source reads each one.

The places theme is read for venue names by the venue and sub-venue recipes, through place-names/names.parquet and poi.db. One row holds both because the register scopes a decision to one publisher in one jurisdiction, and the two themes carry different terms, so a decision records each theme's terms separately. The divisions theme, ODbL 1.0, reaches the corpus through the admin gazetteer's Overture fold: the trailing-region recipes join postcodes to localities in that database, and for Canada and the other countries the fold covers, the locality and region names can be Overture rows.

rows.notes: The on-disk openaddresses/extracted/ch/countrywide.csv is dated 2021-10-17. OpenAddresses switched ch/countrywide to swisstopo's official building address directory only on 2024-11-22 (520f9ebf45a6), so the file the rendered-ch and fragment-assay recipes read is this BFS publication rather than ch-property-building-1.

rows.authority_basis: The IDE, the national spatial data infrastructure under Presidencia de la República, publishes the national geographic address points

rows.authority_basis: The Landesverwaltung keeps the official index of building addresses (amtliches Gebäudeadressverzeichnis) and publishes it on its geodata download service

rows.notes: Read by the llv-li adapter. 12,966 address rows in `dataset.csv` retrieved 2026-10-18, each with street, number, postcode, postal locality and coordinates.

rows.authority_basis: The Land Registry records every registered transfer of land on the Isle of Man and publishes the transactions as open data

rows.notes: Read by the landregistry-im adapter, which keeps only the address columns and emits each distinct address once. 40,847 transactions and 26,748 distinct addresses in `landtransactionsjan2025.csv`.

rows.authority_basis: The Grand Bahama Port Authority administers the City of Freeport under the Hawksbill Creek Agreement and assigns its street addresses

rows.notes: Read by the gbpa-bs adapter. 61,722 Freeport address points in `CSV/addresses.csv`, each with block-and-parcel number, street, city and island. Covers the City of Freeport only.

rows.source: UN/LOCODE, the United Nations Code for Trade and Transport Locations (UNECE Recommendation 16)
rows.owner: United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UNECE)
rows.authority_basis: UNECE maintains UN/LOCODE through UN/CEFACT under Recommendation 16 and publishes each release on unlocode.unece.org
rows.access: Release archive linked from https://unlocode.unece.org/publications/ (MDB, CSV, TXT, XML and SKOS), no key; this host reads `code-list.csv` from the `datasets/un-locode` repackaging on GitHub
rows.notes: No corpus source reads this list. `$MAILWOMAN_DATA_ROOT/un-locode/un-locode.db`, built from it by `@mailwoman/un-locode-lookup`, feeds the UN_LOCODE annotation of the `nominatim` command. Each entry has a country, a three-character location code, a name, a subdivision, an eight-position function classifier (port, rail, road, airport, postal exchange, multimodal, fixed transport, border crossing) and, on most entries, coordinates in degrees and minutes. The terms read on 2026-11-23 limit use to personal, non-commercial use; the decision records each reading.

rows.source: OurAirports open data downloads (airports.csv, runways.csv, countries.csv, regions.csv)
rows.authority_basis: OurAirports, a volunteer-edited airport database founded by David Megginson, publishes a nightly CSV dump of its records
rows.access: CSV files at https://davidmegginson.github.io/ourairports-data/, to which `ourairports.com/data/*.csv` redirects, no key
rows.notes: No corpus source reads these files. `@mailwoman/registry` compiles its IATA and ICAO location codes from `airports.csv` (profile `open-2026-11`), and `mailwoman corpus fetch ourairports` writes the four files for the sub-venue corpus arc. Each airport row has an ident, a type (large, medium and small airports, heliports, seaplane bases, balloon ports, closed sites), a name, a point, an ISO country and region, a municipality and the IATA, ICAO, GPS and local codes; no row has a street address. The site states no seat; the row is filed under CA because the founder's own career page lists the University of Ottawa and the Government of Canada.
